v2.label: Verb in second place
v2.rule: In a normal Dutch statement the conjugated verb is always the second thing in the sentence.

inversion.label: Inversion
inversion.rule: Start with a time or place instead of the subject and the verb still has to be second, so the subject hops behind it.

question.label: Questions
question.rule: Yes or no questions put the verb first. With a question word, the verb comes straight after it. Verbs lose their -t in front of je or jij.

negation.label: niet or geen
negation.rule: Use geen in front of a noun with no article or with een. Everything else is negated with niet.

modals.label: Modal verbs
modals.rule: The modal (kunnen, moeten, mogen, willen) takes second place and sends the other verb to the very end in its base form.

separable.label: Separable verbs
separable.rule: In a main clause the prefix breaks off and goes to the end. It stays attached after a modal, after te, and in a subordinate clause.

imperative.label: Telling someone to do something
imperative.rule: Use the bare stem and put it first. Words like even and alstublieft are what keep it from sounding like an order.

er-is.label: er is and er zijn
er-is.rule: Dutch opens with er to say that something exists. Singular takes er is, plural takes er zijn.

perfect.label: Perfect tense
perfect.rule: The helper verb (hebben or zijn) sits in second place and the past participle drops to the end of the sentence.

past.label: Simple past
past.rule: The past form takes the normal second place. Dutch uses it most for was, had, and for describing how things used to be.

subordinate.label: Subordinate clauses
subordinate.rule: After omdat, dat, als, of and toen every verb walks to the end of its own clause.

conjunctions.label: want, maar and en
conjunctions.rule: want, maar, en and dus join two normal sentences and change nothing. This is why want is the safe choice when omdat scares you.

om-te.label: om ... te
om-te.rule: To say what something is for, wrap the base form in om ... te and park the whole thing at the end.

reflexive.label: Reflexive verbs
reflexive.rule: me, je, zich or ons comes straight after the verb. A lot of Dutch verbs need it where English uses none.

er.label: er with a preposition
er.rule: Dutch never says over het or met het about a thing. It becomes er, and the preposition often slides to the end.

comparative.label: Comparing
comparative.rule: Add -er to compare and -st to top the list. The word for than is dan, never als.

tmp.label: Time, manner, place
tmp.rule: When several details pile up they go in this order: when, how, where.

future.label: Talking about later
future.rule: gaan plus the base form for plans, zullen for promises and offers. The second verb still lands at the end.

passive.label: Passive
passive.rule: worden plus the past participle when the doer does not matter. Official letters are full of it, which is why the exam uses it.

relative.label: die and dat
relative.rule: die for a de-word, dat for a het-word. The clause it opens is a subordinate clause, so its verb goes to the end.

conditional.label: zou
conditional.rule: zou plus the base form is how Dutch gets polite. It is the difference between wanting something and asking for it nicely.

items.en: I live in the Netherlands
items.why: Subject first, then the verb. That is the default shape of a Dutch sentence.

items.en: He works at the town hall
items.why: werkt is in second place, right behind the subject hij.

items.en: She speaks a little Dutch
items.why: The verb stays in slot two and everything else follows it.

items.nl: het kind speelt in de tuin
items.en: The child is playing in the garden
items.why: Dutch has no separate -ing form. One present tense covers plays and is playing.

items.en: I have two children
items.why: hebben in second place. Dutch does not add a word for do or does.

items.en: My husband works in Rotterdam
items.why: mijn man counts as one unit in slot one, so the verb still comes second.

items.nl: de les begint om negen uur
items.en: The lesson starts at nine o'clock
items.why: The subject is three words long but it is still one slot, so begint is second.
accept: om negen uur begint de les

items.nl: ik ben nieuw in de buurt
items.en: I am new in the neighbourhood
items.why: A handy opener when you meet the neighbours. ben is the ik form of zijn.

items.en: We live next to the school
items.why: wij takes the same form as the base verb, wonen.

items.en: I like drinking tea
items.why: Dutch says I drink gladly. graag is how you say you like doing something.

items.nl: de winkel sluit om zes uur
items.en: The shop closes at six o'clock
items.why: Verb second, then the time at the end.
accept: om zes uur sluit de winkel

items.nl: wij drinken koffie in de pauze
items.en: We drink coffee during the break
items.why: Subject, verb, object, then the time phrase.

items.nl: morgen ga ik naar de gemeente
items.en: Tomorrow I am going to the town hall
items.why: morgen took slot one, so the verb keeps slot two and ik moves behind it.
accept: ik ga morgen naar de gemeente

items.en: Today I am working from home
items.why: Starting with the time pushes the subject behind the verb. Never werk ik not: vandaag ik werk.
accept: ik werk vandaag thuis

items.en: After that I go home
items.why: daarna is in slot one, so it is ga ik and not ik ga.
accept: ik ga daarna naar huis

items.en: You may not park here
items.why: hier opens the sentence, the modal mag follows, and the base form parkeren waits at the end.
accept: je mag hier niet parkeren

items.en: I don't have time right now
items.why: Opening with nu flips heb and ik around.
accept: ik heb nu geen tijd

items.nl: in het weekend sporten wij samen
items.en: At the weekend we do sports together
items.why: The whole phrase in het weekend fills slot one, so sporten comes before wij.
accept: wij sporten samen in het weekend
wij sporten in het weekend samen

items.en: I am staying home tonight
items.why: Time first, verb second, subject third.
accept: ik blijf vanavond thuis

items.en: Where do you live?
items.why: Question word, then the verb. And woont loses its -t in front of je.

items.en: What is your name?
items.why: Dutch asks how you are called, not what your name is.

items.en: Do you speak English?
items.why: No question word, so the verb goes first. With u the -t stays on.

items.en: Do you have an appointment?
items.why: Verb first for a yes or no question, and hebt drops to heb in front of je.

items.en: When does the course start?
items.why: Question word, verb, subject. Dutch needs no word for does.

items.en: How many children do you have?
items.why: hoeveel kinderen is one question phrase in slot one, so heeft comes next.

items.en: Why are you here?
items.why: bent is the u form of zijn in a question.

items.en: Could you repeat that?
items.why: Worth knowing by heart for the speaking exam. The base form herhalen sits at the end.

items.en: May I see your passport?
items.why: The modal mag goes first and zien waits at the end.

items.en: How much is a day ticket?
items.why: Dutch asks what it costs rather than how much it is.

items.en: I don't have time
items.why: tijd has no article in front of it, so the negative word is geen.

items.en: He doesn't speak Dutch
items.why: A bare noun gets geen, never niet.

items.en: I don't understand
items.why: het is a definite word, so you negate with niet, and niet comes after it.

items.en: We don't have a car
items.why: een auto becomes geen auto. geen already contains the een.

items.en: That is not my bike
items.why: mijn fiets is definite, so niet does the work and stands in front of it.

items.en: I don't know that man
items.why: niet goes at the end, after the object die man.

items.en: She doesn't work here anymore
items.why: niet meer is the fixed pair for not anymore.

items.en: I have to go to the doctor
items.why: Dutch leaves gaan out after a modal when the direction is obvious.

items.en: You are not allowed to smoke here
items.why: The modal mag is second and roken goes last, with niet just before it.

items.en: I can't come
items.why: kan second, komen at the end, niet in between.

items.en: We want to rent a house
items.why: The object een huis squeezes in between the modal and the base form at the end.

items.en: She has to work tomorrow
items.why: moet in second place, werken right at the back.
accept: morgen moet zij werken

items.nl: ik wil graag een afspraak maken
items.en: I would like to make an appointment
items.why: wil graag is the polite way to ask. maken still drops to the end.

items.nl: je moet eerst een nummer trekken
items.en: You have to take a number first
items.why: Everything piles up between moet and trekken.

items.nl: ik kan vanavond niet naar de les komen
items.en: I can't come to the lesson tonight
items.why: Long middle, but komen still lands at the very end.
accept: vanavond kan ik niet naar de les komen

items.nl: ik sta om zeven uur op
items.en: I get up at seven o'clock
items.why: opstaan splits: sta takes second place and op is left at the end.
accept: om zeven uur sta ik op

items.en: He calls the town hall
items.why: opbellen splits around the object.

items.en: We tidy up the kitchen
items.why: opruimen breaks in two, with op pushed to the back.

items.nl: de trein komt om tien uur aan
items.en: The train arrives at ten o'clock
items.why: aankomen splits and aan waits behind the time.
accept: om tien uur komt de trein aan

items.en: She fills in the form
items.why: invullen splits, which is the verb you meet on every Dutch form.

items.nl: ik neem de telefoon niet op
items.en: I don't answer the phone
items.why: niet slips in just before the loose prefix op.

items.nl: het vliegtuig vertrekt om zes uur
items.en: The plane leaves at six o'clock
items.why: vertrekken looks separable but is not. ver- never breaks off.

items.en: Close the door
items.why: Bare stem first, and dichtdoen still splits with dicht at the end.

items.en: Fill in this form
items.why: The stem vul leads and in drops to the end.

items.en: Please wait a moment
items.why: even and alstublieft are what turn an order into a request.

items.en: Please speak more slowly
items.why: A sentence worth memorising before any speaking test.

items.en: Turn the light off
items.why: uitdoen splits here too, exactly like in a normal sentence.

items.nl: er is een probleem met de verwarming
items.en: There is a problem with the heating
items.why: One problem, so er is. This is the sentence that starts a call to the landlord.

items.nl: er zijn veel mensen in de wachtkamer
items.en: There are a lot of people in the waiting room
items.why: mensen is plural, so er zijn.

items.nl: er staat een fiets voor de deur
items.en: There is a bike in front of the door
items.why: Dutch prefers a real verb like staan or liggen to say where something is.

items.en: There is no wifi here
items.why: er is plus geen for something that is not there.

items.en: There is no lesson today
items.why: er holds slot one so the verb can stay second.
accept: vandaag is er geen les

items.en: I have filled in the form
items.why: heb is second, and the participle ingevuld goes last. Separable verbs wedge ge- inside.

items.en: We ate pizza yesterday
items.why: Dutch uses the perfect where English uses a plain past.
accept: gisteren hebben wij pizza gegeten

items.en: He moved to the Netherlands
items.why: Movement with a destination takes zijn, not hebben.

items.nl: zij heeft de hele dag gewerkt
items.en: She worked all day
items.why: werken takes hebben, and gewerkt ends with a t because k is in 't kofschip.

items.nl: ik ben met de trein gekomen
items.en: I came by train
items.why: komen takes zijn. The participle still waits at the end, behind the how.

items.nl: heb je de brief al gelezen
items.en: Have you read the letter yet?
items.why: A question, so heb goes first, but gelezen still ends the sentence.

items.nl: ik heb mijn paspoort thuis gelaten
items.en: I left my passport at home
items.why: The place thuis comes before the participle, because the participle is always last.

items.nl: de dokter heeft mij medicijnen voorgeschreven
items.en: The doctor prescribed me medicine
items.why: voorschrijven is separable, so ge- lands in the middle: voorgeschreven.

items.nl: wij zijn vorige week naar Utrecht geweest
items.en: We went to Utrecht last week
items.why: geweest is the participle of zijn and it always pairs with zijn.
accept: vorige week zijn wij naar Utrecht geweest

items.nl: hij is gisteren om zes uur opgestaan
items.en: He got up at six o'clock yesterday
items.why: opstaan takes zijn and its ge- sits inside the word: opgestaan.

items.en: It was very cold yesterday
items.why: was and had are the two past forms Dutch really does use in speech.
accept: gisteren was het erg koud

items.nl: vroeger woonde ik in een klein dorp
items.en: I used to live in a small village
items.why: The simple past is the normal choice for how things used to be.
accept: ik woonde vroeger in een klein dorp

items.en: We had no money back then
items.why: hadden is the plural past of hebben.
accept: toen hadden wij geen geld

items.en: I didn't know the answer
items.why: weten is irregular: wist in the past.

items.en: The shop was already closed
items.why: was in second place, just like any other verb.

items.nl: ik blijf thuis omdat ik ziek ben
items.en: I am staying home because I am sick
items.why: After omdat the verb walks to the end: ik ziek ben, not ik ben ziek.

items.nl: ik weet niet of hij komt
items.en: I don't know whether he is coming
items.why: of means whether here, and it sends komt to the end.

items.nl: zij zegt dat ze morgen komt
items.en: She says that she is coming tomorrow
items.why: dat pushes komt right past morgen to the end.

items.nl: als het regent neem ik de bus
items.en: If it rains I take the bus
items.why: The als clause fills slot one, so the main clause flips to neem ik.
accept: ik neem de bus als het regent

items.nl: ik kan niet komen omdat ik moet werken
items.en: I can't come because I have to work
items.why: Both verbs go to the end of the omdat clause: ik moet werken.

items.nl: hij vraagt of u een afspraak heeft
items.en: He asks whether you have an appointment
items.why: heeft travels all the way past the object to the end.

items.nl: ik hoop dat u mij kunt helpen
items.en: I hope that you can help me
items.why: Both verbs end up at the back: kunt helpen.

items.nl: ik ga naar huis want ik ben moe
items.en: I am going home because I am tired
items.why: want changes nothing. Compare omdat, which would force ik moe ben.

items.nl: hij komt niet want hij heeft het druk
items.en: He isn't coming because he is busy
items.why: Two ordinary sentences glued together. het druk hebben is the fixed phrase for being busy.

items.nl: ik wil komen maar ik heb geen tijd
items.en: I want to come but I don't have time
items.why: maar joins two full sentences and leaves both alone.

items.nl: het regent dus ik neem de tram
items.en: It is raining so I am taking the tram
items.why: dus can join two sentences without moving anything.

items.nl: ik ga naar de winkel om brood te kopen
items.en: I am going to the shop to buy bread
items.why: om ... te wraps the reason, and te kopen closes the sentence.

items.nl: hij heeft geen tijd om te sporten
items.en: He has no time to do sports
items.why: With no object in between, om te sits together right at the end.

items.nl: ik bel u om een afspraak te maken
items.en: I am calling you to make an appointment
items.why: The object een afspraak slides in between om and te.

items.nl: het is belangrijk om Nederlands te leren
items.en: It is important to learn Dutch
items.why: After it is plus an adjective, Dutch adds om before te.

items.en: I don't feel well
items.why: zich voelen always needs its pronoun. Say this one at the doctor.

items.en: You have to register first
items.why: With u the pronoun is zich, and it comes straight after the modal.

items.en: He is mistaken
items.why: English has no pronoun here at all, which is exactly why this gets forgotten.

items.nl: wij haasten ons naar het station
items.en: We hurry to the station
items.why: Every subject has its own reflexive word, and wij takes ons rather than zich.

items.en: Are you feeling better already?
items.why: je twice, and both are needed: one is the subject, one is the reflexive.

items.en: She gets dressed quickly
items.why: aankleden is both reflexive and separable, so zich sits in the middle and aan goes last.

items.nl: ik heb me bij de gemeente ingeschreven
items.en: I registered at the town hall
items.why: The reflexive me comes early, the participle ingeschreven comes last.

items.en: I am happy with it
items.why: blij met plus a thing becomes er ... mee, and met changes shape to mee.

items.en: We will talk about it tomorrow
items.why: er and over split apart, with the time word sitting between them.

items.nl: ik heb er geen zin in
items.en: I don't feel like it
items.why: zin hebben in becomes er ... in. A very everyday sentence.

items.nl: hij denkt er nog over na
items.en: He is still thinking about it
items.why: nadenken over is separable too, so three pieces end up spread out: er, over, na.

items.en: What do you think of it?
items.why: Here er and van stay glued together as ervan.

items.nl: deze fiets is duurder dan die
items.en: This bike is more expensive than that one
items.why: duur plus -er, and than is dan.

items.en: My Dutch is getting better and better
items.why: beter is irregular, and steeds is how Dutch says more and more.

items.en: This is the cheapest subscription
items.why: The top of the list takes -ste and the het in front of it.

items.nl: de trein gaat sneller dan de bus
items.en: The train goes faster than the bus
items.why: Comparing two things always uses dan.

items.nl: hij woont dichter bij het station dan ik
items.en: He lives closer to the station than I do
items.why: Dutch stops at dan ik. There is no extra word for do.

items.nl: ik ga morgen met de bus naar mijn werk
items.en: I am going to work by bus tomorrow
items.why: When, then how, then where: morgen, met de bus, naar mijn werk.
accept: morgen ga ik met de bus naar mijn werk

items.nl: zij fietst elke dag naar school
items.en: She cycles to school every day
items.why: Time before place, the opposite of the usual English order.

items.nl: wij gaan zaterdag samen naar de markt
items.en: We are going to the market together on Saturday
items.why: zaterdag is when, samen is how, naar de markt is where.

items.nl: ik heb gisteren met de dokter gebeld
items.en: I called the doctor yesterday
items.why: Time and manner line up in order, and the participle still closes the sentence.

items.nl: hij reist elke week met de trein naar Brussel
items.en: He travels to Brussels by train every week
items.why: All three details at once, in the order when, how, where.

items.en: I am going to move next week
items.why: gaan plus the base form is the everyday way to talk about a plan.
accept: volgende week ga ik verhuizen

items.en: It will rain tomorrow
items.why: zullen plus the base form at the end. Used more for predictions than plans.
accept: morgen zal het regenen

items.en: We will call you tomorrow
items.why: zullen is the form you want when you are promising something.
accept: morgen zullen wij u bellen

items.en: Shall I open the window?
items.why: Zal ik is how you offer to do something. The base form stays whole here.

items.en: Shall we have coffee together?
items.why: Zullen we is the standard way to suggest something.

items.nl: ik moet het formulier nog invullen
items.en: I still have to fill in the form
items.why: After a modal the separable verb stays in one piece at the end.

items.nl: wij komen morgen bij u langs
items.en: We will drop by your place tomorrow
items.why: langskomen splits and langs ends up behind everything else.

items.nl: vergeet niet je pas mee te nemen
items.en: Don't forget to bring your card
items.why: With te, a separable verb splits around it: mee te nemen.

items.en: The cake is being baked
items.why: worden plus the past participle. The baker has disappeared from the sentence.

items.nl: het formulier wordt door de gemeente verwerkt
items.en: The form is processed by the town hall
items.why: If you do name the doer, it comes in with door.

items.nl: de brief is vorige week verstuurd
items.en: The letter was sent last week
items.why: A finished passive uses zijn, not worden.

items.en: No dogs are allowed here
items.why: The sign version. hier takes slot one, so worden comes second.

items.nl: uw aanvraag wordt binnen vier weken behandeld
items.en: Your application will be processed within four weeks
items.why: Straight out of a letter from the town hall, which is why it is worth recognising.

items.nl: het huis wordt volgende maand verkocht
items.en: The house will be sold next month
items.why: Present tense worden can point at the future, just like in English.

items.nl: de man die naast mij woont werkt bij de politie
items.en: The man who lives next to me works for the police
items.why: de man is a de-word, so die. Inside that clause woont goes to the end.

items.nl: het boek dat ik gisteren kocht is heel goed
items.en: The book I bought yesterday is very good
items.why: het boek is a het-word, so dat. English can drop the that, Dutch cannot.

items.nl: de brief die ik kreeg was in het Nederlands
items.en: The letter I got was in Dutch
items.why: die for a de-word, and the main verb was waits until the clause has finished.

items.nl: dit is de vrouw met wie ik werk
items.en: This is the woman I work with
items.why: For a person after a preposition, Dutch uses wie.

items.nl: ik zou graag een afspraak willen maken
items.en: I would like to make an appointment
items.why: zou plus graag is the polite upgrade of ik wil. Two base forms pile up at the end.

items.en: Could you repeat that?
items.why: The politest version of kunt u dat herhalen.

items.en: I wouldn't do it
items.why: zou second, doen at the end, niet in between.

items.nl: als ik meer tijd had zou ik vaker sporten
items.en: If I had more time I would exercise more often
items.why: The als clause sends had to its end, then the main clause flips to zou ik.

items.nl: omdat ik ziek was ben ik niet naar de les gegaan
items.en: Because I was sick I didn't go to the lesson
items.why: The omdat clause fills slot one, so the main clause starts ben ik.

items.nl: nadat ik gegeten had ging ik naar bed
items.en: After I had eaten I went to bed
items.why: Two verbs at the end of the nadat clause, then inversion in the main clause.
accept: nadat ik had gegeten ging ik naar bed

items.nl: hoewel het regende zijn wij toch gaan fietsen
items.en: Although it was raining we went cycling anyway
items.why: hoewel behaves like omdat, and gaan fietsen is a double base form at the end.

items.nl: ik had het formulier eerder moeten opsturen
items.en: I should have sent the form earlier
items.why: Two base forms stack at the end, moeten opsturen, instead of a participle.

items.nl: wij gaan eerst eten en daarna kijken wij een film
items.en: We will eat first and then we will watch a film
items.why: en changes nothing, but daarna starts the second half, so that half inverts.

items.en: Can you help me?
items.why: Verb first, then the person you are asking, with helpen at the end.

items.en: I am looking for the nearest pharmacy
items.why: A long adjective still sits quietly between the article and the noun.

items.en: My neighbour makes a lot of noise
items.why: The opening line of many a complaint.

items.nl: ik heb een klacht over mijn woning
items.en: I have a complaint about my home
items.why: klacht over is the fixed pair. Worth knowing for the housing topics.

items.en: Could you write that down please
items.why: After a modal, opschrijven stays whole at the end.

items.nl: ik begrijp u wel maar ik versta u niet
items.en: I understand you but I can't hear you clearly
items.why: verstaan is hearing the sounds, begrijpen is getting the meaning. The exam tests the difference.

items.en: What time is it?
items.why: Dutch asks how late it is.

items.nl: ik ben vorig jaar naar Nederland gekomen
items.en: I came to the Netherlands last year
items.why: komen takes zijn, and gekomen closes the sentence.
accept: vorig jaar ben ik naar Nederland gekomen

items.nl: mijn zoon zit op de basisschool
items.en: My son is at primary school
items.why: Dutch says sits at school, and school takes op rather than in.

items.en: We have to sort this out together
items.why: oplossen stays whole after the modal and lands at the end.
